clue.text: World Cup team misused toiletry

indicators.note: letters that are misused are put to the wrong use, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football squad at the World Cup has been mishandling its bathroom products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges the twelve letters of WORLD CUP TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc powder is a toiletry dusted on the skin after bathing.

clue.text: Legs at the bottom provide surprises

explanation.surface: Someone's lower limbs keep springing unexpected things on people.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn-ups are the folded-back cuffs at the bottom of trouser legs; a 'turn-up for the books' is a British phrase for a surprise. 'provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser legs end in folded cuffs at the hem, and an unexpected event is informally called a turn-up.

clue.text: Wash and air two foreign articles first

indicators.note: first says the articles come before the word for air in the answer

parts.note: LA is the French for 'the'
UN is the French for 'a'
to air washing is to dry it

explanation.surface: Instructions for doing the washing, then hanging it out, with a strange aside about foreign grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the two French articles, LA and UN, ahead of DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is the batch of clothes being washed, so the noun stands for a wash.

clue.text: Floor covering not fully considered?

parts.note: something not fully considered was felt only partly, i.e. ..., which is also the name of the padding laid beneath a carpet

explanation.surface: A carpet or rug chosen without enough thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Underfelt is the felt layer laid under a carpet; read as UNDER-FELT it means insufficiently felt, so 'not fully considered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Underfelt is carpet underlay, a felt layer forming part of the floor covering.

clue.text: Person in charge of the beginners making lace

parts.note: PIC is an abbreviation of person in charge

indicators.note: the beginners of the two words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Whoever runs a class of novices is also making lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginners' takes the first letters of 'of the', O and T, after PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is one of the small ornamental loops that edge lace, so it stands for a piece of lacework.

clue.text: Transposition for sheepdog — it's elementary

indicators.note: a transposition swaps the two halves of the word built from sheepdog

parts.note: sheep gives RAM and dog gives WOLF, a wild canine

explanation.surface: A sheepdog swap: simple stuff, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'sheepdog' as sheep plus dog, RAM plus WOLF; 'Transposition' swaps the halves, putting WOLF before RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a chemical element.

clue.text: He prophesied a swing cutting out gin and port

indicators.note: cutting out means the word for gin is removed from the word for a swing

parts.note: a trapeze is an acrobat's swing
a gin is a snare or trap
Kiel is a German Baltic port

explanation.surface: A prophet foretells a political swing that will see the end of gin and port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting out' removes TRAP from TRAPEZE, leaving EZE. 'gin' wants to be the drink, but here it is the hunter's snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezekiel was the Hebrew prophet of the Old Testament book named after him.

clue.text: Accept the consequences with boldness, opposing factions in charge

parts.note: face means effrontery or boldness, as in having the face to ask
THEM and US are two opposing sides

explanation.surface: A leader steps up to take the blame, bravely, while rival groups run things.
explanation.definitionFit: To face the music is an idiom for confronting the unpleasant results of one's actions.

clue.text: Stranded silver ring

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a circle or ring

explanation.surface: A silver ring left stuck somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run onto the bottom is stranded, unable to float free.

clue.text: Part of a mass or amass

explanation.surface: A question of grammar: piece of a mass, or the verb amass?
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short prayer read in the Mass; to collect is to gather together.
explanation.definitionFit: The collect is a set prayer in the church service, and gathering things together is to accumulate them.

clue.text: Heathen trend must be frustrated immediately

indicators.note: frustrated plans are thrown into disorder, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion among pagans needs to be stopped at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be frustrated' rearranges the letters of HEATHEN TREND.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something there and then means doing it on the spot, without delay.

clue.text: Country's currency encountering trouble — a run on it

parts.note: the ecu was a European currency unit
ado means fuss or trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A nation's money hits difficulty and then suffers a run on the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a run on it' tacks the run on at the end; 'encountering' is a link. The ecu was the European currency unit used before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American nation, a country on the equator.

clue.text: Insect's name I note

parts.note: a term is a word or name for something
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on what a bug is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A termite is a social insect that eats wood, sometimes called a white ant.

clue.text: Tart of the fishy sort?

parts.note: a huss is a dogfish sold in British chip shops, so a fish-like version of that word, with a y on the end, names a brazen woman

explanation.surface: A pastry dish made with seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like pastry, but it means an immoral woman; huss is the British fishmonger's name for dogfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussy is an impudent or immoral woman, which is what tart means in slang.

clue.text: Menial elf working in the home

indicators.note: working here means being worked over into a new form, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lowly fairy is busy doing chores about the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of MENIAL ELF into the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: En famille is French for within the family, so at home among one's relatives.

clue.text: In burning heat, pies rise and crack

indicators.note: In puts the turned word for pies inside the word for burning heat

parts.note: fire is heat that burns

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word for pies reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: tarts are pies

explanation.surface: Baking in a hot oven, the pastry swells and splits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns the pies upwards and 'In' puts them inside the heat. 'crack' looks like the pies splitting, but it is the adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack as an adjective means top-quality or excellent, as in a crack regiment.

clue.text: Party man has brought leaders of District Health Authority into the affair

indicators.note: into means the initials go inside the word for affair

parts.note: a matter is an affair or business

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A partygoer has pulled the local health officials into some business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party man' is not a politician: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland; 'has brought' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's Mad Hatter is the host of the famous mad tea-party, so a party man.

clue.text: Dot embraces a boy, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: embraces means the word for dot holds the boy's name inside it

parts.note: in Morse code a dot is spoken as dit
Alec is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl called Dot hugs a lad, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name, but it is the Morse dot, DIT. 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional form of a language, a local way of talking.

clue.text: For rent, see below

explanation.surface: A property listing: available to let, details underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' here is the past participle of rend, meaning torn apart; 'see below' read as a cross-reference is 'as under'. 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rent is torn into pieces, and a note pointing to what follows says the same as 'see further down'.

clue.text: Transport has to keep moving to and fro

parts.note: to wag is to move from side to side, as a tail does
on means continuing, as in to keep going

explanation.surface: A vehicle has to stay rocking back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'wag on' is to keep wagging; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled vehicle for carrying goods.

clue.text: Fish's colouring

explanation.surface: The hue of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiting is a sea fish of the cod family, and also powdered chalk used as whitewash.
explanation.definitionFit: The whiting is a cod-like food fish, and whiting is also ground chalk used for whitewashing walls.

clue.text: Giant pig holding his end up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction reads from bottom to top
holding means the word for pig wraps around the word for his end

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a pig's back end is its tail

explanation.surface: A huge pig is holding its rear in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the tail inside the pig, giving HTAILOG; 'up' reverses it all, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath is the Philistine giant of the Bible slain by David with a sling.

clue.text: In the Letters of St. Paul, a broad blade

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: In the Epistles of Saint Paul, a wide sword is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like St Paul's Epistles, but 'Letters of' asks for the letters of ST PAUL A, rearranged. 'In the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a kitchen or medical tool with a flat, wide implement head.

clue.text: French town where Danish Secretary of State hid

definitions.text: where Danish Secretary of State hid

explanation.surface: A town in France where a Danish politician went into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: Arras is a town in northern France; in Hamlet, Polonius, adviser to the Danish king, hides behind an arras (a tapestry wall hanging) and is stabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arras is a town in northern France, and an arras is the tapestry curtain behind which Polonius concealed himself in Hamlet.

clue.text: Threesome allowed to' go on tour

parts.note: to trip is to take a journey or excursion
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A trio given permission to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'to' is a printing mark; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is a set of three, such as three notes played in the time of two.

clue.text: About to try swallowing divine cheese

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for try takes in the letters for divine

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine

explanation.surface: A clergyman is about to sample a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective praising the cheese, but it is a clergyman, abbreviated DD (Doctor of Divinity). Cheddar is a hard English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese named after the Somerset village.

clue.text: Living in Sherman, I'm a Texan

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from Texas says he lives in Sherman, a town in that state.
explanation.definitionFit: Animate means alive, as opposed to inanimate objects.

clue.text: Not being familiar with slang term that almost baffled

indicators.note: baffled means confused and thrown about, so the letters before it are rearranged
almost means the word that loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a slang expression because they have never come across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts THAT to THA; 'baffled' rearranges SLANG, TERM and THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping someone at a distance means holding back from intimacy or friendliness.
